name: Vance Athletic Rundown (Gen 9, Distressed)
description: A Tier 2 athletic shoe — the Vance Gen 9 — that has worked its way down to the Shelf through secondhand markets, charity drops, and outright theft. By the time a pair reaches Tier 1, the cushioning is compressed flat, the upper is creased and stained, and the original colorway is a memory. Some pairs have been re-laced with cord or wire. They're still identifiable by the embossed 'V' on the heel, now worn smooth.
what_it_says: You're wearing someone else's cast-offs. That's not a judgment — it's just the chain of things.
worn_by: anyone who scored them at a drop
resellers who kept a pair for themselves
story_hooks: Inside the heel of one pair, wedged under the insole, is a folded piece of paper with a door code.
Vance Athletic's loyalty program chip is still active. The original owner is still alive — and looking for these shoes.

physical_description.visual_profile: A once-premium athletic silhouette now reduced to functional minimalism. The shoe maintains its recognizable form—low-top runner with flared heel counter—but the aesthetic has shifted entirely toward weathered utility. The overall impression is of something stripped down by time and hard use, familiar yet diminished.
physical_description.fit: Snug around the midfoot with a relaxed toe box. The midsole has compressed considerably, sitting lower than original spec. Lacing sits loose in worn eyelets; the shoe conforms more to the foot's actual shape than intended engineering.
physical_description.primary_material: Fused synthetic mesh upper with ballistic weave reinforcement at toe and heel. Midsole is compressed EVA foam showing separation at the sole seam. Outsole is vulcanized rubber worn thin at the heel strike zone.
physical_description.texture: Creased and cracked mesh with a matte finish where gloss has worn away. The heel counter is soft from compression, no longer rigid. Sole shows exposed midsole foam in high-wear areas. Eyelets are dulled metal or plastic. The embossed 'V' heel tab is smooth and almost illegible.
physical_description.color_scheme: Original colorway faded to uncertain grays and subdued blue-gray. Visible staining: coffee brown on the lateral side, dark salt marks around the toe, possible rust streaks from wire lacing. The heel counter retains a ghost of the original cobalt accent line.
physical_description.closures: Standard eyelets with mixed cord—some original synthetic laces frayed and knotted at breaks, others replaced with paracord or bare wire twisted through the top eyelets for durability.
distinctive_features: Embossed 'V' on heel counter, worn smooth and barely legible
Visible midsole separation at the toe box
Mixed lacing materials indicating field repairs
Heel strike wear exposing foam layers
Creasing patterns mapping foot architecture and gait
Faded brand stitching on the tongue, almost ghosted
Possible hand-stitched repairs at the toe or sides
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 salvage/Tier 2 original. Now inhabited by Tier 5 or desperate Tier 4 users. The brand heritage signals former status, but condition screams sub-grade reality.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by the Shelf—people who cannot afford new and cannot return them. Signals street survival, economic precarity, and rejection of throwaway culture through necessity. Someone wearing these either cannot afford Tier 3+ footwear or has chosen the authenticity of aged utility over newness.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily weathered. Compression permanent. Multiple repair attempts visible. Staining and discoloration are expected. Not broken—still functional—but clearly end-of-life for Tier 2 standards, early-life for Tier 5 wearers.
